statements.text: E_G is the gravitational self-energy of the difference between the two mass distributions of a superposition: for a rigid displacement, the energy it costs to move one component, in the gravitational field of the other, from coincidence to its displaced position.

$E_G$ is the gravitational self-energy of the difference between the two mass distributions of a superposition: for a rigid displacement, the energy it costs to move one component, in the gravitational field of the other, from coincidence to its displaced position.

sources.quote: EG is the gravitational self-energy of the difference between the two (stationary) mass distributions of the superposition
